questions.text: Do you work, or are you a student?

questions.text: Describe a person you know who is very good at cooking.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a person you know who is very good at cooking. You should say: who this person is; what kind of food they cook; how you know about their cooking; and explain why you think this person is so good at cooking.

questions.text: Have you ever cooked a meal together with this person?
questions.say: Thank you. Have you ever cooked a meal together with this person?

questions.text: Why do some people enjoy cooking while others don't?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a person you know who is very good at cooking, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all cooking at home. Why do some people enjoy cooking while others don't?

questions.text: Do you think children should learn to cook at school? Why or why not?
questions.say: Do you think children should learn to cook at school? Why or why not?

questions.text: How has the way families eat at home changed in recent years?
questions.say: How has the way families eat at home changed in recent years?

questions.text: Why are ready meals and food delivery so popular nowadays?
questions.say: Now let's talk about food and convenience. Why are ready meals and food delivery so popular nowadays?

questions.text: What are the disadvantages of eating fast food regularly?
questions.say: What are the disadvantages of eating fast food regularly?

questions.text: Do you think people will cook less in the future?
questions.say: Do you think people will cook less in the future?
